literature_notes: All six ledger lines (L1–L6) describe the same experimental system: full-length IGSF3 carrying a C-terminal V5 tag ('IGSF3-V5') or a C-terminal FLAG tag ('IGSF3-FLAG') expressed in B16 or 293FT cells. IGSF3 is a Type I single-pass transmembrane protein: the large ectodomain spans residues 20–1124 (after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 19), the TM helix spans 1125–1147, and the cytoplasmic tail spans 1148–1194. A C-terminal tag therefore lands on the intracellular face, not the extracellular surface. The immunofluorescence detection of IGSF3-V5 at cell–cell contact sites (L4) is consistent with permeabilized-cell staining of an intracellular epitope, which is standard practice; the ledger clip does not state live-cell or non-permeabilized surface staining. No ledger line describes an N-terminal extracellular tag, an internal loop insertion, a snorkel construct, or any tag placed in the extracellular span (residues 20–1124). Because no ledger line supports an extracellular surface tag insertion, zero sites are reported.

literature_other_positions.note: IGSF3-V5 is a C-terminal V5 fusion; the C-terminus (residue 1194, D) lies in the cytoplasmic tail (residues 1148–1194) and is therefore intracellular, not surface-accessible.
IGSF3-FLAG is a C-terminal FLAG fusion used in the same co-IP experiment; the C-terminus is equally intracellular and does not qualify as an extracellular surface tag site.
